title: Backlog: Explain safe recovery from refused Dolphin and Proton setup state
body:
## Audit-discovered follow-up

From #603 verified blind/refutation review, G-04/G-28. Severity: Low improvement.

Dolphin safely refuses a reserved GC copy stage after an interrupted first seed, and Steam safely refuses unknown/incomplete existing Proton versions. Those preservation decisions are intentional. Current messages name paths or ask users to resolve the version, but the supported inspection/recovery instructions need a clear home. A leftover name alone never establishes safe deletion; do not automatically discard unknown player files.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes. Synthetic isolated fixtures can exercise these paths without a handheld, personal library, credentials or provider account. Runtime requires a fresh root-owned serialized allocation with original exits and bounded cleanup.

Already written: preserve existing player files and historical original results. No deployed owner state is repaired or erased by filing this task.

Owner: M7 integrator. Priority: later documentation/recovery improvement; not a private H700 test gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document exact refusal states, what remains preserved, how to inspect the named paths and when a separately confirmed removal is safe; no blanket delete instructions.
- [ ] Any changed player-visible copy updates canonical flow/IA and exact-source screenshots under D-WORKFLOW-155/156; unchanged safe-refusal behavior is explicit.
- [ ] Link the guidance from the appropriate support surface when available without making website deployment a private firmware gate.


## Explicit #612 audit disposition

**Deferred, not fixed.** Owner: M7 integrator. Priority: P3, backlog recovery guidance; before any related recovery UI change. Milestone: unassigned backlog. Intentionally refused unknown retained state remains protected. Clearer recovery guidance is a separate documentation/UI task, with flow/frames required for any screen change; no unsafe automatic deletion is introduced for audit closure.

Applicability evidence: `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-15-h700-audit-applicability/`, actual current077197 SYSTEM and generated menu, successful run20261015T220831Z-ed601ef5; all original exits0. This does not inspect retained device overrides or authorize deployment.
